also: I’ll tell you when I have any news

terms.grammar: quid with the partitive genitive novī, “what of new?”
evidence: Plin. Ep. 3.14.6: quid praetereā novī? Nihil (Lewis & Short s.v. subjungō)
Traupman 104: is there any news?, num quid novī?
terms.comment: News in Latin is “something new”: aliquid novī, nihil novī, with the neuter genitive. The noun “news”, a report of events, is nūntius.

evidence: Franmorarius, Dē variīs fōrmulīs XXV.2 (loci collection; not classical)
Traupman 104: is there any news?, num quid novī?
terms.comment: Numquid expects the answer no or leaves it open: “there isn’t any news, is there?”

phrases.latin: Sī quid forte novī habēs dē eā rē …
phrases.english: If you happen to have any news about it …
I’ll tell you when I have any news.
